findings.claim: Signed favorable-minus-comparison endpoint contrasts at the observed selection nodes are strongest and most reproducible for the short-range pair kernels: pair_kernel_1.5 (integrated z 0.562, q 1.5e-4, positive batch fraction 1.0), pair_kernel_2.5 (0.631, q 2.2e-5, 1.0) and pair_kernel_3.5 (0.540, q 9.8e-5, 1.0), with pair_kernel_5.0 weaker (0.319, q 3.7e-3) and pair_kernel_7.0 reversed (-0.485, q 1.5e-4, positive batch fraction 0.0). The same ordering appears in the raw and adjusted branch correlations (pair_kernel_1.5 r=0.085/0.101, pair_kernel_2.5 r=0.088/0.084, pair_kernel_7.0 r=-0.055/-0.050). This is selection enrichment of a radial pair-distance shell density, not an absolute geometric descriptor and not an interaction energy.

Shape anisotropy carries signed contrast information beyond the centroid: shape_yy is the most negative endpoint contrast (integrated z -0.513, q 1.5e-5, positive batch fraction 0.0) and remains negative after branch adjustment (r=-0.103 raw, -0.100 adjusted, q 3e-4), while shape_xx (-0.495, q 8.1e-4) and shape_yz (-0.212, q 0.035) are weaker and shape_xz is positive (+0.185, q 0.22, not significant). The corresponding regional local_cyy enrichment is negative at every landmark (e.g. landmark_00 -0.575, landmark_07 -0.646, landmark_16 -0.672, landmark_19 -0.622, all q<2e-3), so the yy-compression signal is spatially broad rather than localized to one region.

Global centroid coordinates show no reproducible signed endpoint contrast: global_centroid_x -0.111 (q 0.26), y -0.243 (q 0.014 but positive batch fraction 0.21) and z -0.061 (q 0.48), and after branch adjustment all three collapse (adjusted correlations -0.010, +0.010, -0.016, all q>0.38). Centroid displacement is therefore not supported as a favorable direction on this evidence.

Landmark soft-minimum distances and radial-shell occupancies carry opposite signs at the same landmark, so they are not interchangeable proxies. At landmark_00 the softmin contrast is negative (-0.481, q 8.1e-4) while occupancy3 is positive (+0.545, q 2.4e-4) and occupancy5 positive (+0.208, q 0.020); the same pattern recurs at landmark_02 (softmin +0.253 vs occupancy3 -0.038, occupancy5 -0.323), landmark_06 (softmin +0.294 vs occupancy3 -0.009, occupancy5 -0.365), landmark_15 (softmin +0.369 vs occupancy5 -0.357) and landmark_18 (softmin +0.264 vs occupancy5 -0.311). Lower soft-min distance and higher shell occupancy are different observables and cannot be averaged into one target.

The supplied continuous contrast functions are observed-node linear interpolants over the complete observed window [0.0,0.49] with extrapolation disallowed, and they are not monotone: landmark_00_soft_mass has 4 sign changes with first_rate_z +9.27 and last_rate_z -10.00, landmark_00_local_dx has 6 sign changes (first -17.49, last +8.11), and landmark_00_local_cxy has 9 sign changes with relative node RMSE 0.867. A constant rule and a time-conditioned rule therefore differ materially on these curves, and the curves are contrasts, not absolute reward targets.

Fit fidelity is weak for these curves: no polynomial was accepted (polynomial_accepted false for all landmark_00 and landmark_01 features), relative node RMSE ranges roughly 0.29-1.00, and the curve_support audit reports last empirical z and last fit z of opposite sign for many selected features (e.g. landmark_00_occupancy3 empirical -0.040 vs fit +0.545; landmark_02_occupancy5 +0.142 vs -0.323; landmark_16_occupancy5 +0.315 vs -0.175) with 0-15 strong sign-conflict nodes. The fitted curve should not be treated as a validated description of the observed contrast.

Parent-child increment contrasts disagree in sign with the population endpoint contrasts for several features: landmark_00_softmin increment rate z is -4.91 (q 0.046) matching the negative population contrast, but landmark_00_occupancy3 increment is +4.28 (q 0.081) and landmark_02_occupancy5 increment is -1.55 (q 0.38) while its population contrast is also negative; shape_xx increment is -3.70 (q 0.095) and shape_yy -3.85 (q 0.16), consistent in sign with the endpoint shape effects, whereas shape_xz increment is +3.00 (q 0.21) against a positive endpoint contrast. Within-path change and changing cohort composition are not separable from these tables alone.

Turnover accounting shows large positive residual rates for the same features that carry the strongest endpoint contrasts: landmark_00_local_cxx residual +4.29 (q 0.038), landmark_00_local_cyy +5.05 (q 0.033), landmark_01_local_cyy +6.40 (q 0.014), landmark_04_local_cxx +5.67 (q 0.012), landmark_07_local_cxx +5.08 (q 0.012), landmark_16_local_cyy +6.37 (q 0.012), landmark_17_local_cxx +5.24 (q 0.012) and landmark_19_local_cxx +5.30 (q 0.012), each with positive batch fraction 0.79-1.0. These residuals are accounting diagnostics that mix score reclassification and extant-parent weighting; they are not causal selection effects and not atom velocities.

Joint diagnostics separate coherent from marginal structure: selection innovation aligns with native alignment (0.092, q 2.2e-9, positive batch fraction 1.0) and with the teacher innovation contrast (0.226, q 2.2e-9, 1.0), while it is negatively associated with observed child score gain (-0.036, q 1.8e-7, positive batch fraction 0.0). The teacher contrast decomposes into internal fraction 0.787, translation fraction 0.132 and rotation fraction 0.081, with atom participation fraction 0.384. These are descriptive within-selector associations with batch as the independent unit, not causal module evidence.

Joint-motion RMS features are the most reproducible negative branch-adjusted effects: joint_innovation_RMS_A -5.15e-5 (q 0.038 raw, q 0.020 adjusted, same-sign batch fraction 0.86/0.93), joint_internal_RMS_A -5.00e-5 (q 0.044/0.030, 0.79/0.93) and joint_translation_RMS_A -1.10e-5 (q 0.095/0.072, 0.71/0.71), with adjusted correlations -0.150, -0.137 and -0.076. Because the adjusted branch covariance is supplied evidence, these are motion-residual diagnostics rather than region moments, and they do not establish a causal benefit.

The information audit bounds what the teacher evidence can support: compressed-choice excess fixed-frame RMS is 0.081 A (CI 0.070-0.092) against a fixed RMS of 0.564 A and proper-rigid RMS of 0.529 A, top-4 teacher overlap is 0.470 (CI 0.427-0.515), and chosen-teacher score correlations are small (compressed 0.102, full 0.064). Teacher control root ESS is 1.30, teacher lower-rejected fraction 0.326 and teacher sign-calibration cosine 0.973. These are observational teacher-score associations, not a fitted or independently validated affinity predictor.

Descendant credit is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity: decoded_terminal_learning_labels_available is false, the label semantics are recorded affinities removed with an equal score prior, and the lineage table covers 700 batch nodes over [0.0,0.5] with 349 nodes having fewer than 3 ancestors and 531 fewer than 6, so ancestral coverage is thin and survivor bias is not removable. Last-record credit must not be presented as final affinity benefit, and the unavailable terminal comparison is reported as unavailable.

hypotheses.claim: Testable coordinate hypothesis: the favorable direction is a shift of the pair-distance distribution toward the 1.5-3.5 A shell and away from the 7.0 A shell, observable as pair_kernel_1.5/2.5/3.5 increasing and pair_kernel_7.0 decreasing at the observed selection nodes. Intended response is a signed increase in the endpoint contrast for the short-range kernels; target origin is the observed selection-node population; spatial scale is 1.5-3.5 A pair separation; temporal scale is the complete observed window [0.0,0.49]. Discriminating failure condition: pair_kernel_1.5/2.5/3.5 contrasts fail to increase, or pair_kernel_7.0 increases, under the same evaluation. This is a measurable contrast, not an absolute target, and the executing pointcloud scalar has no pair-kernel term, so it remains descriptive unless a permitted reward recipe can express it.

Testable coordinate hypothesis: reducing the yy component of the shape tensor (shape_yy) while leaving shape_xz and the centroid free is associated with the favorable contrast. Observable is the signed shape_yy endpoint contrast; intended response is a more negative shape_yy contrast; target origin is the observed selection-node population; spatial scale is the global shape tensor in Angstrom squared; temporal scale is the complete observed window. Discriminating failure condition: shape_yy contrast becomes non-negative or loses batch reproducibility while shape_xz or centroid contrasts move instead. The surrounding coordinates that should retain freedom are the centroid and the off-diagonal shape components, since their contrasts are weak or non-significant.

Testable temporal hypothesis: a time-conditioned contrast rule is preferable to a constant rule for the landmark_00 and landmark_01 features, because the observed-node curves change sign repeatedly within [0.0,0.49] (4-10 sign changes) and the fitted curves disagree in sign with the last empirical node for many features. Observable is the sign and magnitude of the observed-node contrast at each score time; intended response is agreement between the rule and the observed-node interpolation; target origin is the observed selection-node population; temporal scale is the complete observed window with no extrapolation. Discriminating failure condition: a constant rule matches the observed-node signs as well as the time-conditioned rule, or the time-conditioned rule requires extrapolation beyond [0.0,0.49].

Testable accounting hypothesis: the large positive turnover residuals for the shape and local-covariance features reflect score reclassification and extant-parent weighting rather than within-path coordinate change, because the parent-child increment contrasts for those features are smaller in magnitude and often opposite in sign to the population contrasts. Observable is the difference between population rate and edge rate for each feature; intended response is a residual that shrinks when parent weighting is held fixed; target origin is the observed selection-node population; temporal scale is the complete observed window. Discriminating failure condition: the residual persists at the same magnitude when reclassification and parent weighting are held fixed, which would instead support within-path change. The residual is an accounting diagnostic, not a causal selection effect.

Testable joint-geometry hypothesis: coherent joint coordinate patterns, not isolated marginal descriptors, carry the reproducible signal, because selection innovation aligns with native alignment and teacher innovation contrast while joint_innovation_RMS_A and joint_internal_RMS_A are the most reproducible negative branch-adjusted effects. Observable is the joint innovation RMS and its alignment with the teacher contrast; intended response is a decrease in joint innovation RMS with preserved internal coherence; target origin is the observed selection-node population; spatial scale is the whole active slot set; temporal scale is the complete observed window. Discriminating failure condition: isolated marginal descriptors reproduce the effect while joint innovation RMS does not change, or the joint effect disappears when the internal fraction is held fixed.

Testable landmark hypothesis: the soft-minimum distance and the radial-shell occupancy at the same landmark encode different information and should be treated as separate observables, because their endpoint contrasts have opposite signs at landmark_00, landmark_02, landmark_06, landmark_15 and landmark_18. Observable is the pair of signed contrasts at each landmark; intended response is that a change moving softmin in the favorable direction does not simultaneously move occupancy3/occupancy5 in the same direction; target origin is the observed selection-node population; spatial scale is the 5 A landmark neighborhood with sigma 1 A shells; temporal scale is the complete observed window. Discriminating failure condition: softmin and occupancy contrasts move together with the same sign at every landmark, which would indicate a single redundant descriptor.

limitations: Descendant credit is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity; decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable.
Turnover residual includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not only resampling, and is not a causal selection effect.
Adjusted branch covariance is supplied evidence; region moments themselves are not rigid-motion residuals.
Curve fitting does not establish causal benefit or a gradient; no time bins or outside-window analysis was performed.
Static teachers are last-learning-node forecasts, not actual final structures.
All weak and null scalar effects were retained; current study outcomes are withheld from design roles.
The executing pointcloud scalar has no pair-kernel, moment, joint-motif or geometry-block term, so pair-kernel and shape findings remain descriptive unless a permitted reward recipe expresses them.
Temperatures are immutable task parameters and were not proposed or edited.
